positive.query: Calculate our CAC and CAC payback by channel from this marketing spend and new customer data.
Prepare our LTV, LTV to CAC ratio and contribution margin for the board, and tell me whether our customer acquisition is profitable.
Work out contribution margin per order and how many repeat orders it takes to recover acquisition cost for our ecommerce store.

nearMiss.query: Estimate the TAM, SAM and SOM for project management software for construction firms in North America.
Design good, better, best pricing tiers and packaging for our new analytics product.
Explain why marketing spend came in 18% over budget last quarter.

holdout.query: Show how payback period and LTV change if churn doubles or CAC rises 20% for our small business segment.

scenarios.task: A hypothetical subscription software company has 4 months of history. ARPA is 500 per month. Reported gross margin is 80%, but customer support and onboarding salaries are booked in operating expense. Paid media last quarter was 300,000 and sales and marketing salaries were 300,000; the company won 100 new customers, 40 of them organic. Observed monthly churn is 1% so far. The CEO wants to tell investors LTV is 40,000 and LTV:CAC is above 6. Build the unit economics, correct what needs correcting, and state what can and cannot be concluded.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline accepts the reported gross margin, uses paid-only blended CAC, repeats the 40,000 LTV from 1% churn over 4 months of data, and endorses the ratio against an invented industry benchmark.

scenarios.task: Hypothetical data: paid search spent 100,000 and won 50 customers; paid social spent 150,000 and won 25 customers; ARPA is 400 per month and gross margin 75%. Management sees a blended payback and wants to double paid social. Compare channels, compute payback for each, and give a sensitivity view before recommending.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline reports only a blended figure and approves doubling paid social without channel payback, marginal CAC, or sensitivity.
